fields.description:
## Context / Problem

The configuration surface and the per-run correlation identity exist but nothing reaches the
wire: rebar still sends no request headers, so a gateway cannot attribute or group gate
calls. Header values also sit adjacent to `provider_provenance`, which is written into
verdicts and sidecars (`src/rebar/llm/findings.py:122-123`,
`src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py:339`), so delivery without redaction would place
operator-supplied values into durable records.

## Approach

Resolve `${run:...}` references and place the finished headers on the call through
pydantic-ai's `ModelSettings.extra_headers`, by extending the dict returned from
`build_model_settings` (`src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:338`), whose result flows to the
model call at `src/rebar/llm/runner.py:567`.

That seam rather than the transport: one insertion covers every provider that supports
`extra_headers`, whereas patching transport would need edits at both
`src/rebar/llm/providers.py:295` and `src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py:155` and would still miss
non-httpx providers. `build_model_settings` is already a pure function with a purity test
(`tests/unit/test_structured_run_seam.py`) and reads config exactly as `max_tokens` does.

Headers are attached only when `cfg.base_url` is set. A configured intermediary is the only
topology in which these headers mean anything — verified inert when sent directly to
`api.anthropic.com` — and gating on it prevents an operator's internal correlation or
routing values from being transmitted to a public provider endpoint. This reuses the
condition `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py:554` already treats as "an intermediary is present"
when it flips provenance `tier` to `best_effort`. Consequence to accept: rebar's Bedrock path
takes no `base_url`, so headers are inert there.

Redaction: header names are recorded, values never are. `provider_provenance` gains at most
the sorted list of configured header names, and every log or diagnostic path renders values
as a fixed placeholder.

**An absent `${run:...}` substituend omits the whole header.** Only two scopes mint a run
identity — `workflow/gate_dispatch.py:167` and `:762`. `review-code` opens no `gate_config`
scope and has no ticket, so those values are absent there, as for any standalone op. Such a
header is dropped rather than sent empty: an empty correlation header pollutes the gateway, and
raising would break every standalone op merely because headers are configured globally —
observability must never break an operation, the rule `tracing.py` already follows.

Deliberately asymmetric with the unset-`${env:VAR}` hard error: an env var is knowable at
config time, so its absence is an operator mistake, whereas a run value's absence is legitimate
runtime context — not every operation is a gate run.

Validation is re-applied after `${run:...}` substitution: those references resolve at call
time, so a value that passed config validation is not yet proven safe. Re-running the same
name/value checks on the finished header closes the validate-before-substitute gap here too.

**Pass a fresh `dict(...)` per call, never the config-held mapping.** At the pinned pydantic-ai
1.107.2 the Chat Completions path reads `model_settings.get('extra_headers', {})` with NO copy
(`models/openai.py:1001`) and then `.setdefault('User-Agent', ...)` (`:1002`), mutating the
caller's dict — unlike the Responses path (`:2300`) and `models/anthropic.py:772`, which both
copy first (upstream bug 6866, fixed after this pin). Verified live in this checkout: a supplied
`{"x-corp-tag": "rebar"}` came back carrying `User-Agent`. Handing over the config's own dict
would therefore pollute it across calls and leak a pydantic-ai version string into the recorded
header-name set, making a signed verdict's provenance non-deterministic. This is the exact path
`base_url` selects, so the copy is required, not defensive style.

**Bedrock carries no headers at this pin.** `models/bedrock.py` has zero `extra_headers`
references at 1.107.2 despite `settings.py` listing it, so headers are inert there. The
`base_url` gate already excludes that path, so behavior is unaffected; the sibling docs ticket
records the limitation.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py` — add `extra_headers` to the assembled model settings.
- `src/rebar/llm/headers.py` — `${run:...}` resolution against the run identity.
- `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` — record header names, never values, in provenance.
- `tests/unit/test_header_delivery.py` (new) — the tests below.

## Testing

Tier: a contract test that drives the real assembly seam and captures what it hands the
boundary, plus in-process unit tests for resolution. The correlation assertion must capture
the headers **from the real call site** — the dict `build_model_settings` actually returns —
rather than recomposing the resolution helpers, because a re-derived oracle stays green if
the call site later stops calling them, which is the only regression the test exists to
catch.

- Happy path: with `base_url` and a `${run:trace_id}` header configured, the settings dict
  returned inside a gate run carries the resolved value.
- Edge path: with no `base_url`, the settings dict carries no `extra_headers` key at all.
- Edge path: with no headers configured, the settings dict is byte-identical to today's.
- Failure path: an unknown `${run:bogus}` reference raises `LLMConfigError` naming the key.
- Redaction path: a sentinel header value is absent from captured log output and from the
  serialized `provider_provenance`, while its header name is present.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With `base_url` set and headers configured, the dict returned by
      `build_model_settings` contains `extra_headers` with the resolved values; checked by a
      test calling the real function inside a gate-run scope and asserting on its return
      value, not on recomposed helpers.
- [ ] Every call in one gate run carries the same `${run:trace_id}` value and two runs differ;
      checked by a test capturing the settings dict from repeated calls in one scope and from
      a second scope.
- [ ] With `base_url` unset, no `extra_headers` key is present; checked by a test asserting
      the key is absent from the returned dict.
- [ ] With no headers configured, the returned dict equals the dict produced before this
      change; checked by a test comparing against an explicitly constructed expected dict.
- [ ] A header whose value only becomes unsafe after `${run:...}` substitution is rejected
      with `LLMConfigError`; checked by a test forcing a run value containing CR, LF or NUL
      and asserting the raise, proving validation re-runs on the substituted result.
- [ ] A header carrying `${run:...}` is omitted entirely outside a gate run rather than sent
      empty; checked by a test resolving headers for a standalone op and asserting the key is
      absent from `extra_headers` while a sibling literal header is still present.
- [ ] The configured headers mapping is not mutated by a model call; checked by a test asserting
      the config's dict is byte-identical before and after a request, which fails against the
      pinned upstream no-copy path if the copy is dropped.
- [ ] A configured header overrides a same-named client default rather than being dropped;
      checked by a test asserting the configured value reaches the request, pinning the merge
      precedence that is the most-regressed behaviour in comparable projects.
- [ ] An unknown `${run:...}` key raises `LLMConfigError` naming the offending key; checked by
      `pytest.raises` asserting the key appears in the message.
- [ ] A sentinel header value appears in no log record and in no serialized
      `provider_provenance`, while the header name does appear; checked by a test using
      `caplog` and a serialized provenance record.
